prompt: Write an email to a colleague about a new hobby you have taken up. Aim for about 400 words. Reply with the email only.
final_message:
Subject: A new hobby, and a jar on my counter

Hi Dana,

I wanted to tell you about something I've taken up, since you were kind enough to listen to me complain about my weekends last month. I've started baking sourdough bread. I know half the country did this a few years ago and I'm late to the party, but I'm here now and I have flour on the floor to prove it.

It began when my neighbor gave me a jar of her starter, which is a bubbly paste of flour and water that you have to feed like a very small pet. She handed it over and said it was nearly impossible to kill. I'd like her to know I came close. The first week I forgot it on the counter for three days, and I was sure I'd ruined it. It sulked for a bit and then came right back, which is more than I can say for most of my houseplants.

My first loaf came out about as dense as a doorstop. I sliced it anyway and ate a piece with butter, and I'll admit it tasted better than it had any right to. The second loaf was a little better, and the third rose properly and had a crust that crackled when I set it on the rack. I stood in the kitchen listening to it for a good minute, feeling very pleased with myself.

What I like most is that it can't be hurried. You mix things in the evening, leave them alone overnight, and shape the dough in the morning. There's a lot of waiting, and I've found I don't mind it. I used to fill every spare minute with something, and now I sit with my coffee and let the dough do its work. My husband says the house smells like a bakery, which I take as high praise, since he usually only notices the smell of burnt toast.

I'm no expert, and I make plenty of mistakes. I still can't get the slashes on top to look like the pictures in the books. Mine come out looking more like a scribble than a pattern. But the bread is good, and I'm learning something each time.

I'd like to bring you a loaf on Friday, if you'll have it. I'll warn you that it may be a lopsided one, but it will be a warm one, and I promise it won't be the doorstop.

Hattie
